title: Guelph Innovation District block plan for Blocks 1 and 2
subtitle: Park size, employment land, school location, Frost Building heritage notice and stormwater design were all decided.
overview: Council held a special meeting on the Block Plan for Blocks 1 and 2 of the Guelph Innovation District, proposed by Fusion Homes for lands at 328 Victoria Road South and 588 Stone Road East. Staff had recommended refusing the plan as submitted and setting conditions for endorsement. Council instead approved the applicant's plan as amended, with conditions that staff must be satisfied are met.

Council did not adopt staff's requirements for a community park of at least 6.7 hectares or 16.48 hectares of employment mixed-use land; both were defeated {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m4}}. That leaves the applicant's smaller community park and reduced employment land in place. Council did require the elementary school to sit outside employment land and next to parkland with no road between {{vote:m7}}. The Frost Building may not be in a park block {{vote:m10}}. A single-loaded road along the eastern edge was kept {{vote:m11}}, and stormwater design must satisfy the City Engineer {{vote:m12}}.

Council also authorized notice of intention to designate the Frost Building under the Ontario Heritage Act {{vote:m20}}. If the modifications are not made to staff's satisfaction, the plan returns to Council. Endorsement allows planning applications to follow, with public notice and meetings.

decisions.detail: Council approved the applicant's block plan for Blocks 1 and 2, instead of refusing it as staff recommended, subject to the amendments adopted that night {{vote:m15}}.
Council defeated the requirement for a community park of at least 6.7 hectares {{vote:m3}}.
Council defeated the requirement for at least 16.48 hectares of employment mixed-use land {{vote:m4}}.
The school must be outside employment mixed-use land, meet school board sizing and phasing needs, and sit next to parkland with no dividing road {{vote:m7}}.
The Frost Building must not be located in a park block, leaving its eventual use and zoning open {{vote:m10}}.
Council required a single-loaded road along the eastern edge of Blocks 1 and 2, next to the Eramosa River valley {{vote:m11}}.
Any revisions needed to stormwater facilities must be made to the City Engineer's satisfaction {{vote:m12}}.
The Clerk may publish notice of intention to designate the Frost Building under the Ontario Heritage Act, with a designation by-law to follow if no objections arise {{vote:m20}}.

debate: Staff said the applicant's community park was about half the recommended size and could not hold sports fields, a cricket pitch and parking. They said the linear neighbourhood parks were too narrow for playgrounds or courts under zoning frontage and setback rules, and that trails cannot count as parkland dedication.

The applicant's team argued that parkland should be spread through the neighbourhood so every home is within walking distance of a park. They said staff's plan puts most of it in one place and that the overall parkland amount was equivalent. A cycling advocacy delegate supported the linear parks for active transportation. Some councillors raised the growing demand for cricket and sports fields.

On employment land, staff said the plan cut it well below the secondary plan's intent and that a school in an employment designation does not conform to policy. The applicant said the land is poorly suited to manufacturing and offered a mix of retail, a school and a possible innovation hub. Another delegate urged keeping employment land for its local supply-chain and tax benefits.

Councillors questioned how firmly the school board had approved the school site. The applicant said planning staff at the board had confirmed it by email. A councillor noted this was not a decision of the board itself and raised safety concerns about a road between school and park.

On the Frost Building, staff and the applicant disagreed about putting it in a park block, since staff saw no city use for it. Some councillors favoured adaptive reuse and heritage conservation. Another said the building should not be kept at all.
